hints: Notice the real directions at the kite: $W$ is vertically down and $T$ pulls down to the left along the string, so $F$ must push up to the right.
For three coplanar forces in equilibrium the free vectors must join head-to-tail into a closed triangle with $W+T+F=0$.
Check each triangle for closure and for which diagonal is $T$: the $T$ side must continue the loop in the opposite sense to $F$ and represent the down-left string pull.
walkthrough: Identify the forces at the kite: $W$ vertically down, $T$ along the string down to the left, and unknown wind force $F$.
Use the equilibrium rule for coplanar forces: the vector sum is zero, so the three free vectors must form a closed triangle when joined head-to-tail.
Since $W$ and $T$ both have downward components, $F$ must have an upward component to cancel them, so $F$ is directed up to the right.
Slide the vectors without changing direction: $W$ down, then $F$ up-right from the tip of $W$, then $T$ back to the start gives a triangle pointing to the right.
Only the diagram with $W$ on the left, $F$ as the lower up-right side and $T$ as the upper side closing the loop in the correct sense satisfies this.

options.A: Forms a closed head-to-tail triangle with $W$ down, $T$ down to the left along the string and $F$ up to the right, so $W+T+F=0$ for equilibrium.
options.B: Has the same shape as the closed triangle but the arrow on $T$ is reversed, so the three vectors do not circulate head-to-tail to zero.
options.C: Places $W$ and $F$ so the upper diagonal labelled $T$ does not give the required down-to-the-left pull of the string in the closed loop.
options.D: Interchanges $T$ and $F$ on the two diagonal sides, so the string tension is shown acting in the direction required for the wind force.
